defects: Hypothesis is strengthened compared to gold: `(l.filter p).length ≤ 1` requires at most one *position* in the list to satisfy p (counting multiplicity), whereas gold's `{x ∈ l₁ | p x}.Subsingleton` only requires at most one *distinct value* satisfying p among the (deduplicated) set of elements. E.g. l = [a, a] with p a = true satisfies gold's hypothesis (the set {x ∈ l | p x} = {a} is a singleton, hence Subsingleton) but violates the produced hypothesis (l.filter p = [a, a] has length 2), so the produced theorem applies to a strictly smaller class of lists than the gold theorem — it is a weaker/less general statement.

Uses `List.find` (a plain, non-Option-returning finder) rather than `List.find?`, which gold and Lean core actually use for this Bool-predicate search; `List.find` with this signature/behavior does not correspond to a standard current declaration, raising doubt about whether the statement even elaborates as intended.
